```{python}
# ── what varies between the batches ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── small shared derivations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def html_section(title, *blocks):
    """A titled section only the HTML render shows.

    The computational output — the tables the calls are read off, the marker counts, the
    split diagnostics — belongs in the document but not on a slide: pandoc puts printed
    output on a slide of its own as raw monospace text.

    Emitted as one markdown block, which is load-bearing. A fenced div opened in one
    display() call and closed in another is not paired up: each call is its own block, so
    the fence survives into the deck as literal ":::" text on a slide of its own.
    """
    body = "\n\n".join(str(block) for block in blocks)
    display(Markdown(
        f'::: {{.content-visible when-format="html"}}\n\n## {title}\n\n{body}\n\n:::'
    ))


def as_table(frame):
    """A DataFrame or Series as markdown, so it lands as a table rather than as a dump."""
    return frame.to_markdown()


def as_text(lines):
    """Preformatted lines, for output that is not a table."""
    return "```\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n```"


def slide(heading):
    """Emit a slide heading. Every slide function starts with one, so the loop's list of
    slide functions is the deck's table of contents."""
    display(Markdown(f"## {heading}"))


def draw_order(adata):
    """Cells are drawn in this order, so whatever comes last sits on top. Shuffled,
    because the matrix order is the order cells came off the sequencer and it buries
    whole clusters under their neighbours."""
    return np.random.default_rng(0).permutation(adata.n_obs)


def obs_palette(adata, key):
    """The palette scanpy stored in uns, as the dict seaborn wants. Only scanpy reads the
    _colors entry, so seaborn has to be handed it explicitly — otherwise a category
    changes colour between the UMAP and the violins."""
    return dict(zip(adata.obs[key].cat.categories, adata.uns[f"{key}_colors"]))


def recolour_by_position(ax, order, palette):
    """seaborn colours violin bodies in an order that does not follow the x positions when
    hue repeats x, so the legend ends up right and the violins wrong. Recolour each body
    from the category it actually sits under. The order comes off the categorical rather
    than the tick labels, which are empty on a shared axis."""
    for body in ax.collections:
        extents = body.get_paths()[0].get_extents()
        body.set_facecolor(palette[order[round((extents.x0 + extents.x1) / 2)]])


def violin_by_cluster(ax, frame, ranked_key, value_key, label, palette, order):
    """One row of a stacked per-cluster violin figure."""
    # dodge=False because hue repeats x: left on, seaborn gives each cluster its own
    # sub-slot and every violin is drawn a twentieth of its slot wide, off its tick
    sns.violinplot(data=frame, x=ranked_key, y=value_key, hue=ranked_key, palette=palette,
                   legend=False, dodge=False, cut=0, density_norm="width", inner="box",
                   inner_kws=violin_inner_kws, linewidth=0.5, saturation=1, ax=ax)
    recolour_by_position(ax, order, palette)
    ax.set_ylabel(label, fontsize=7)
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=6)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#b0b0b0", linewidth=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


def txn1_violin(ax, frame, hue_key, palette, cell_type_order):
    """Txn1 per cell type, split by one design factor."""
    sns.violinplot(data=frame, x="cell_type", y="TXN1", order=cell_type_order, hue=hue_key,
                   palette=palette, cut=0, density_norm="width", inner="box",
                   inner_kws=violin_inner_kws, linewidth=0.5, ax=ax)
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.set_ylabel("Txn1 (log1p)", fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, labelsize=8)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#b0b0b0", linewidth=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    for label in ax.get_xticklabels():
        label.set_ha("right")
    ax.legend(title="", fontsize=7, frameon=False, loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))


def horizontal_colorbar(fig, ax, bar_ax):
    """The colorbar strip under a UMAP panel. The strip reserves the space; the colorbar
    drawn inside it is excluded from the layout so its tick labels cannot push the panel
    around."""
    bar_ax.axis("off")
    colorbar_ax = bar_ax.inset_axes([0.325, 0.82, 0.35, 0.18])
    colorbar_ax.set_in_layout(False)
    colorbar = fig.colorbar(ax.collections[0], cax=colorbar_ax, orientation="horizontal")

    # placed explicitly at the ends and middle: the automatic locator picks its own round
    # numbers per panel, so the tick count and positions would differ from panel to panel
    low, high = ax.collections[0].get_clim()
    ticks = np.linspace(low, high, 3)
    colorbar.set_ticks(ticks, labels=[f"{tick:.2f}" for tick in ticks])
    colorbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)


# ── the analysis, per batch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def cluster_batch(adata, batch):
    """Subset to one batch, QC it, embed it, and sweep Leiden across resolutions.

    Cached to disk: the sweep is the expensive step and nothing above it varies.
    """
    clustered_path = Path(f"data/processed/GSE150703_adata_{batch}_clustered.h5ad")
    if clustered_path.exists():
        return sc.read_h5ad(clustered_path)

    batch_adata = adata[adata.obs["batch"] == batch].copy()
    for column in ["condition", "timepoint", "sort", "lab", "replicate", "batch"]:
        batch_adata.obs[column] = batch_adata.obs[column].cat.remove_unused_categories()

    batch_adata.var["mt"] = batch_adata.var_names.str.startswith("MT-")
    batch_adata.var["ribo"] = batch_adata.var_names.str.startswith(("RPS", "RPL"))
    batch_adata.var["hb"] = batch_adata.var_names.str.startswith(("HBA-", "HBB-"))
    sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(
        batch_adata,
        qc_vars=["mt", "ribo", "hb"],
        expr_type="log1p",
        percent_top=None,
        log1p=False,
        inplace=True,
    )

    sc.pp.filter_genes(batch_adata, min_cells=3)
    sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(batch_adata, n_top_genes=2000, flavor="seurat")
    sc.pp.pca(batch_adata, svd_solver="arpack")
    sc.pp.neighbors(batch_adata, n_neighbors=10, n_pcs=40)
    sc.tl.umap(batch_adata)

    for resolution in [0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5]:
        sc.tl.leiden(
            batch_adata,
            resolution=resolution,
            key_added=f"leiden_res_{resolution:.2f}_v0",
            flavor="igraph",
            random_state=0,
        )

    batch_adata.write_h5ad(clustered_path)
    return batch_adata


def rank_clusters(adata, resolution):
    """Relabel the chosen resolution's clusters 1..n by size, and return that key."""
    leiden_key = f"leiden_res_{resolution:.2f}_v0"
    ranked_key = f"leiden_res_{resolution:.2f}_v1"

    cluster_sizes = adata.obs[leiden_key].value_counts()
    ranked_labels = [str(rank) for rank in range(1, len(cluster_sizes) + 1)]

    adata.obs[ranked_key] = (
        adata.obs[leiden_key]
        .map(dict(zip(cluster_sizes.index, ranked_labels)))
        .astype("category")
        .cat.reorder_categories(ranked_labels)
    )
    adata.uns[f"{ranked_key}_colors"] = [
        mcolors.to_hex(plt.cm.tab20.colors[(int(label) - 1) % 20]) for label in ranked_labels
    ]
    return ranked_key


def correlate_with_reference(adata, ranked_key, reference_centroids):
    """Spearman correlation of every cluster against every reference class.

    Correlated over the query's variable genes rather than everything shared: the
    housekeeping bulk is near-identical in every class and only lifts all twelve
    correlations together, flattening the differences the call is made on.

    Spearman, so a class is matched on the order it puts the genes in rather than on
    absolute levels — the two datasets were normalized by different pipelines. Ranking the
    rows and taking Pearson is the same thing, and does every pair in one call.
    """
    feature_genes = [
        gene for gene in adata.var_names[adata.var["highly_variable"]]
        if gene in reference_centroids.var_names
    ]

    clusters = adata.obs[ranked_key].cat.categories
    cluster_profiles = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            np.asarray(adata[adata.obs[ranked_key] == cluster, feature_genes].X.mean(axis=0)).ravel()
            for cluster in clusters
        ],
        index=clusters, columns=feature_genes,
    )
    reference_profiles = pd.DataFrame(
        reference_centroids[:, feature_genes].X,
        index=reference_centroids.obs_names, columns=feature_genes,
    )

    ranked_clusters = cluster_profiles.rank(axis=1)
    ranked_reference = reference_profiles.rank(axis=1)
    correlation = pd.DataFrame(
        np.corrcoef(ranked_clusters, ranked_reference)[:len(ranked_clusters), len(ranked_clusters):],
        index=cluster_profiles.index, columns=reference_profiles.index,
    )
    return correlation, len(feature_genes)


def score_markers(adata):
    """Score the marker panel over the cells, and report what of it this batch carries."""
    markers_present = {}
    report = []
    for cell_type, genes in retina_markers.items():
        present = [gene.upper() for gene in genes if gene.upper() in adata.var_names]
        sc.tl.score_genes(adata, gene_list=present, score_name=f"score_{cell_type}")
        markers_present[cell_type] = present
        report.append(f"{cell_type}: {len(present)}/{len(genes)} markers")
    return markers_present, report


def refine_cell_types(adata, ranked_key, cluster_calls, marker_calls, cell_type_palette):
    """Split clusters that hold two classes, where the split is clean enough to believe.

    The reference calls a whole cluster one class, so a population that never forms its
    own cluster cannot be named — the vascular cells in WR_Joyal are one cluster of 106
    holding both endothelium and pericytes. Where the panel and the reference name a
    cluster differently, its cells are split: each goes to whichever of the two scores is
    higher, provided that score clears zero. score_genes centres a score on a control gene
    set, so above zero means enriched above background; a cell clearing neither keeps the
    cluster's call rather than being sent one way on noise.

    A disagreement says where to look, not what to do: the panels are not on a common
    scale, so a panel of bright genes annexes cells from a dim one wherever the two are
    compared. The split is therefore only applied where the cluster actually looks like
    two populations. The test is the L in the scatter, written as a number — in a mixed
    cluster the two scores trade off, so their rank correlation runs negative; in one
    population with a depth gradient both rise and fall together and it runs positive.
    The scores have to actually trade off, not merely fail to correlate: a cluster sitting
    at zero has them independent, which is a cloud rather than an L.
    """
    rival_calls = marker_calls.map(
        {panel.replace("_", " "): cls for panel, cls in marker_to_class.items()}
    )
    refinements = {
        cluster: (cluster_calls[cluster], rival_calls[cluster])
        for cluster in cluster_calls.index
        if cluster_calls[cluster] != rival_calls[cluster]
    }

    diagnostics = []
    for cluster, (parent_class, child_class) in refinements.items():
        in_cluster = (adata.obs[ranked_key] == cluster).to_numpy()
        parent_score = adata.obs[class_scores[parent_class]].to_numpy()
        child_score = adata.obs[class_scores[child_class]].to_numpy()

        reassigned = in_cluster & (child_score > parent_score) & (child_score > 0)
        n_cluster = int(in_cluster.sum())
        n_child = int(reassigned.sum())

        tradeoff = np.corrcoef(
            pd.Series(parent_score[in_cluster]).rank(),
            pd.Series(child_score[in_cluster]).rank(),
        )[0, 1]
        smallest_arm = min(n_child, n_cluster - n_child)
        applied = bool(
            tradeoff < MAX_TRADEOFF
            and smallest_arm >= max(MIN_ARM_CELLS, MIN_ARM_FRACTION * n_cluster)
        )

        if applied:
            if child_class not in adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.categories:
                adata.obs["cell_type"] = adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.add_categories([child_class])
            adata.obs.loc[reassigned, "cell_type"] = child_class

        diagnostics.append({
            "cluster": cluster, "parent": parent_class, "child": child_class,
            "cells": n_cluster, "would move": n_child,
            "tradeoff": round(tradeoff, 3), "applied": applied,
        })

    # a class added above lands at the end of the categories, which would put it last on
    # every axis downstream rather than in with the rest
    adata.obs["cell_type"] = adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.remove_unused_categories()
    adata.obs["cell_type"] = adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.reorder_categories(
        sorted(adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.categories)
    )
    adata.uns["cell_type_colors"] = [
        cell_type_palette[cell_type] for cell_type in adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.categories
    ]
    return refinements, pd.DataFrame(diagnostics)


# ── the slides ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def umap_sweep_slide(adata, resolution_keys):
    """Slide: the Leiden sweep, three resolutions per figure."""
    slide("Leiden sweep")
    order = draw_order(adata)

    for start in range(0, len(resolution_keys), 3):
        group = resolution_keys[start:start + 3]

        # the second row is the colorbar strip the score UMAPs use. It is reserved here
        # too, and left empty, so both sets of panels have identical geometry.
        fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 3, height_ratios=[1, 0.22], figsize=(8.6, 3.4),
                                constrained_layout=True)
        for ax, leiden_key_v0 in zip(axs[0], group):
            sc.pl.umap(adata[order], color=leiden_key_v0, ax=ax, legend_loc="on data",
                       legend_fontsize=9, frameon=True, show=False)
            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="datalim")

        for bar_ax in axs[1]:
            bar_ax.axis("off")
        for empty_ax in axs[0][len(group):]:
            fig.delaxes(empty_ax)

        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)


def umap_clusters_slide(adata, ranked_key):
    """Slide: the chosen resolution's clusters, numbered on the embedding."""
    slide("Clusters on the UMAP")
    # scanpy builds the figure here, and takes no figsize argument, so rcParams is where
    # its size has to be set
    plt.rcParams["figure.figsize"] = (5.0, 4.3)

    ax = sc.pl.umap(adata[draw_order(adata)], color=ranked_key, legend_loc="on data",
                    legend_fontoutline=2, frameon=True, show=False)
    ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="datalim")
    plt.show()


def qc_violin_slide(adata, qc_df):
    """Slide: the batch's per-cell QC, one violin per metric."""
    slide("QC metrics")
    batch_color = adata.uns["batch_colors"][0]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(qc_metrics), squeeze=False, figsize=(9, 3.0),
                             constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, (qc_key, qc_label) in zip(axes.flat, qc_metrics.items()):
        sns.violinplot(data=qc_df, y=qc_key, color=batch_color, cut=0, density_norm="width",
                       inner="box", inner_kws=violin_inner_kws, linewidth=0.5, ax=ax)
        ax.set_ylabel(qc_label, fontsize=9)
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)
        ax.grid(axis="y", color="#b0b0b0", linewidth=0.6)
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def qc_violin_by_cluster_slide(adata, qc_df, ranked_key):
    """Slide: the same QC metrics, split by cluster."""
    slide("QC metrics by cluster")
    palette = obs_palette(adata, ranked_key)
    order = list(adata.obs[ranked_key].cat.categories)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(qc_metrics), 1, squeeze=False, sharex=True, figsize=(9, 4.3),
                             constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, (qc_key, qc_label) in zip(axes.flat, qc_metrics.items()):
        violin_by_cluster(ax, qc_df, ranked_key, qc_key, qc_label, palette, order)

    axes[-1][0].set_xlabel("Cluster", fontsize=9)
    axes[-1][0].tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8)
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def heatmap_reference_slide(reference_correlation):
    """Slide: cluster-to-class correlation, three normalizations.

    The raw correlations sit in a narrow band, so the two scaled panels are what can
    actually be read: down a column asks "which cluster is most this class", and across a
    row asks "which class best fits this cluster" — the annotation question, and the one
    the calls are taken from.

    Only the row scaling is a call. A column's brightest cell is the best home for that
    class whether or not the class is present at all: RPE peaks on a rod cluster in
    WR_Joyal, which says where it would land rather than that it was found.
    """
    slide("Correlation with the reference by cluster")

    class_range = reference_correlation.max(axis=0) - reference_correlation.min(axis=0)
    scaled_by_class = reference_correlation.sub(
        reference_correlation.min(axis=0), axis=1
    ).div(class_range, axis=1)

    correlation_range = reference_correlation.max(axis=1) - reference_correlation.min(axis=1)
    scaled_by_cluster = reference_correlation.sub(
        reference_correlation.min(axis=1), axis=0
    ).div(correlation_range, axis=0)

    panels = {
        "Spearman correlation": reference_correlation,
        "Scaled per class": scaled_by_class,
        "Scaled per cluster": scaled_by_cluster,
    }
    heatmap_panels(panels, scaled_by_cluster, "Reference class", figsize=(9, 4.3))


def score_violin_by_cluster_slide(adata, score_df, ranked_key):
    """Slide: every marker score, split by cluster, six panels per figure."""
    slide("Marker scores by cluster")
    palette = obs_palette(adata, ranked_key)
    order = list(adata.obs[ranked_key].cat.categories)

    for start in range(0, len(score_keys), 6):
        group = score_keys[start:start + 6]
        group_types = list(retina_markers)[start:start + 6]

        fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(group), 1, squeeze=False, sharex=True, figsize=(9, 4.3),
                                 constrained_layout=True)
        for ax, score_key, cell_type in zip(axes.flat, group, group_types):
            violin_by_cluster(ax, score_df, ranked_key, score_key,
                              f"{cell_type.replace('_', ' ')} score", palette, order)

        axes[-1][0].set_xlabel("Cluster", fontsize=9)
        axes[-1][0].tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8)
        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)


def umap_scores_slide(adata):
    """Slide: every marker score on the embedding, three per figure."""
    slide("Marker scores on the UMAP")

    for start in range(0, len(score_keys), 3):
        group = score_keys[start:start + 3]

        fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 3, height_ratios=[1, 0.22], figsize=(8.6, 3.4),
                                constrained_layout=True)
        for ax, bar_ax, score_key in zip(axs[0], axs[1], group):
            sc.pl.umap(adata, color=score_key, ax=ax, frameon=True, colorbar_loc=None,
                       show=False)
            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="datalim")
            horizontal_colorbar(fig, ax, bar_ax)

        for empty_ax in axs[0][len(group):]:
            fig.delaxes(empty_ax)
        for empty_bar_ax in axs[1][len(group):]:
            empty_bar_ax.axis("off")

        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)


def dotplot_markers_slide(adata, markers_present, ranked_key):
    """Slide: the marker panel itself, gene by cluster."""
    slide("Marker genes by cluster")
    # figsize is deliberately not passed: dotplot derives its own from the gene and cluster
    # counts, and forcing it to slide dimensions packs the genes until the dots overlap
    sc.pl.dotplot(adata, markers_present, groupby=ranked_key, standard_scale="var")


def heatmap_panels(panels, diagonal_source, xlabel, figsize):
    """Draw one matrix several ways, columns ordered so the matches read as a diagonal.

    Walk the clusters in order and take each one's best column; a column already placed is
    skipped, and any column no cluster leads with is appended.
    """
    column_order = []
    for cluster in diagonal_source.index:
        best = diagonal_source.loc[cluster].idxmax()
        if best not in column_order:
            column_order.append(best)
    column_order += [name for name in diagonal_source.columns if name not in column_order]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(panels), squeeze=False, figsize=figsize,
                             constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, (title, matrix) in zip(axes.flat, panels.items()):
        # xticklabels/yticklabels left at "auto" thins the labels to every other one once a
        # third panel is on the figure, which leaves half the columns unnamed
        sns.heatmap(matrix[column_order], cmap="viridis", linewidths=0.5, linecolor="white",
                    xticklabels=True, yticklabels=True,
                    cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.6, "pad": 0.02}, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, fontsize=8)
        ax.set_ylabel("Cluster", fontsize=8)
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, labelsize=7)
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelrotation=0, labelsize=7)
        for label in ax.get_xticklabels():
            label.set_ha("right")

    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def heatmap_scores_slide(mean_scores):
    """Slide: mean marker score per cluster, three normalizations.

    The raw means show magnitude, scaling down a column asks "which cluster is most this
    cell type", and scaling across a row asks "which cell type best fits this cluster" —
    the annotation question.
    """
    slide("Marker score heatmap")

    scaled_by_type = (mean_scores - mean_scores.min()) / (mean_scores.max() - mean_scores.min())
    row_range = mean_scores.max(axis=1) - mean_scores.min(axis=1)
    scaled_by_cluster = mean_scores.sub(mean_scores.min(axis=1), axis=0).div(row_range, axis=0)

    panels = {
        "Mean score": mean_scores,
        "Scaled per cell type": scaled_by_type,
        "Scaled per cluster": scaled_by_cluster,
    }
    heatmap_panels(panels, scaled_by_cluster, "Cell type", figsize=(9, 4.3))


def refine_scatter_slide(adata, refinements, diagnostics, ranked_key, cell_type_palette):
    """Slide: the two scores against each other, one panel per candidate.

    A cluster worth splitting looks like an L — each arm high on one score and flat on the
    other, with the middle empty. A diffuse cloud across the diagonal means the two classes
    are not separable this way, and the cluster is left alone.
    """
    slide("Cells reassigned by marker score")
    if not refinements:
        display(Markdown("No cluster was called differently by the reference and the panel."))
        return

    applied = dict(zip(diagnostics["cluster"], diagnostics["applied"]))

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(refinements), squeeze=False,
                             figsize=(4.3 * len(refinements), 3.6), constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, (cluster, (parent_class, child_class)) in zip(axes.flat, refinements.items()):
        in_cluster = (adata.obs[ranked_key] == cluster).to_numpy()
        cluster_cells = sc.get.obs_df(
            adata, keys=[class_scores[parent_class], class_scores[child_class], "cell_type"],
        )[in_cluster]

        for called_class in [parent_class, child_class]:
            is_called = (cluster_cells["cell_type"] == called_class).to_numpy()
            ax.scatter(
                cluster_cells[class_scores[parent_class]][is_called],
                cluster_cells[class_scores[child_class]][is_called],
                s=14, c=cell_type_palette[called_class], linewidths=0,
                label=f"{called_class} ({is_called.sum()})",
            )

        # the decision boundary is the diagonal, which is the whole point of comparing the
        # two scores rather than cutting one of them at a number
        span = [
            cluster_cells[[class_scores[parent_class], class_scores[child_class]]].min().min(),
            cluster_cells[[class_scores[parent_class], class_scores[child_class]]].max().max(),
        ]
        ax.plot(span, span, color="#b0b0b0", linewidth=1.0, linestyle="--", zorder=0)

        ax.set_title(f"Cluster {cluster} — {'split' if applied[cluster] else 'left whole'}",
                     fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xlabel(f"{parent_class} score", fontsize=8)
        ax.set_ylabel(f"{child_class} score", fontsize=8)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
        ax.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False, loc="upper right")

    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def umap_cell_types_slide(adata):
    """Slide: the called cell types on the embedding."""
    slide("Cell types on the UMAP")
    plt.rcParams["figure.figsize"] = (6.5, 4.3)

    ax = sc.pl.umap(adata[draw_order(adata)], color="cell_type", frameon=True, show=False)
    ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="datalim")
    plt.show()

def txn1_violin_celltype_slide(adata, txn1_df, cell_type_palette):

def txn1_violin_condition_slide(adata, txn1_df):

    slide("Txn1 by cell type and condition")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.5), constrained_layout=True)

def txn1_violin_timepoint_slide(adata, txn1_df):
    """Slide: Txn1 per cell type, P14 against P17."""
    slide("Txn1 by cell type and timepoint")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.5), constrained_layout=True)
    txn1_violin(ax, txn1_df, "timepoint", obs_palette(adata, "timepoint"),
                list(adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.categories))
    plt.show()

def umap_txn1_stratified_slide(adata):
    """Slide: Txn1 on the embedding, one panel per design cell.

    Laid out like the violin slides: timepoint down the rows, condition across the
    columns, so the same comparison sits in the same direction in every Txn1 figure.
    """
    slide("Txn1 across the design")
    condition_order = list(adata.obs["condition"].cat.categories)
    timepoints = list(adata.obs["timepoint"].cat.categories)

    umap_coords = adata.obsm["X_umap"]
    txn1 = sc.get.obs_df(adata, keys=["TXN1"])["TXN1"].to_numpy()
    txn1_low, txn1_high = txn1.min(), txn1.max()

    # drawn with scatter rather than sc.pl.umap: it puts the whole embedding underneath in
    # grey, and it fixes the point size, which scanpy scales by cell count — the sparse
    # panels would otherwise carry much larger points than the dense ones.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(timepoints), len(condition_order), squeeze=False,
                             figsize=(5.6, 4.4), constrained_layout=True)
    fig.get_layout_engine().set(w_pad=0.01, h_pad=0.01, wspace=0.01, hspace=0.02)
    for row, timepoint in enumerate(timepoints):
        for column, condition in enumerate(condition_order):
            ax = axes[row][column]
            in_stratum = (
                (adata.obs["timepoint"] == timepoint) & (adata.obs["condition"] == condition)
            ).to_numpy()

            # every cell in grey, so each panel is read against the same outline rather
            # than appearing to be a differently-shaped dataset
            ax.scatter(umap_coords[:, 0], umap_coords[:, 1], s=1, c="#bfbfbf", linewidths=0)
            points = ax.scatter(umap_coords[in_stratum, 0], umap_coords[in_stratum, 1], s=1,
                                c=txn1[in_stratum], cmap="viridis",
                                vmin=txn1_low, vmax=txn1_high, linewidths=0)

            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="datalim")
            ax.set_ylabel(f"Txn1 — {timepoint}" if column == 0 else "", fontsize=8)
            ax.set_title(condition if row == 0 else "", fontsize=9)
            ax.text(0.02, 0.98, f"n={in_stratum.sum():,}", transform=ax.transAxes,
                    va="top", ha="left", fontsize=7)
            ax.set_xticks([])
            ax.set_yticks([])

    colorbar = fig.colorbar(points, ax=axes, location="right", shrink=0.35, pad=0.02, aspect=25)
    ticks = np.linspace(txn1_low, txn1_high, 3)
    colorbar.set_ticks(ticks, labels=[f"{tick:.2f}" for tick in ticks])
    colorbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)

    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def txn1_violin_stratified_slide(adata, txn1_df):
    """Slide: Txn1 per cell type, condition within timepoint.

    Grouped violins rather than four panels: NORM and OIR sit side by side within each cell
    type's slot, so the comparison is a glance rather than a jump between figures.
    Timepoint is the facet, which leaves the interaction readable down a column.
    """
    slide("Txn1 by cell type across the design")
    stratified_violins(adata, txn1_df, facet_key="timepoint", hue_key="condition")


def txn1_violin_stratified_by_condition_slide(adata, txn1_df):
    """Slide: the same data with the roles swapped.

    P14 and P17 side by side within each cell type, and condition as the facet. Reading
    down a column here compares the two timepoints within a condition, where the plot above
    compares the two conditions within a timepoint.
    """
    slide("Txn1 by cell type across the design, grouped by timepoint")
    stratified_violins(adata, txn1_df, facet_key="condition", hue_key="timepoint")


def stratified_violins(adata, txn1_df, facet_key, hue_key):
    """Txn1 per cell type, one facet per level of `facet_key`, grouped by `hue_key`."""
    cell_type_order = list(adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.categories)
    facets = list(adata.obs[facet_key].cat.categories)
    hue_order = list(adata.obs[hue_key].cat.categories)
    palette = obs_palette(adata, hue_key)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(facets), 1, squeeze=False, sharex=True, sharey=True,
                             figsize=(9, 5.0), constrained_layout=True)
    for row, (ax, facet) in enumerate(zip(axes.flat, facets)):
        in_facet = txn1_df[txn1_df[facet_key] == facet]
        sns.violinplot(data=in_facet, x="cell_type", y="TXN1", order=cell_type_order,
                       hue=hue_key, hue_order=hue_order, palette=palette,
                       gap=0.1, cut=0, density_norm="width", inner="box",
                       inner_kws=violin_inner_kws, linewidth=0.5, saturation=1,
                       legend=(row == 0), ax=ax)
        ax.set_ylabel(f"Txn1 — {facet}", fontsize=8)
        ax.set_xlabel("")
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=6)
        ax.grid(axis="y", color="#b0b0b0", linewidth=0.6)
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)
        sns.despine(ax=ax)

    axes[0][0].legend(title="", fontsize=7, frameon=False,
                      loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))
    axes[-1][0].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, labelsize=8)
    for label in axes[-1][0].get_xticklabels():
        label.set_ha("right")

    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
```

## Download

```{python}
#| label: download
# the counts this document analyses, and the annotated reference its cell types are called
# against. Both are fetched once and left on disk; re-rendering re-uses them.
source_urls = {
    "dge": (
        "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE150nnn/GSE150703/suppl/"
        "GSE150703_retina_NORM_OIR_P14_P17_C57_WR_CD73FT_noamg_normalizedUMI_Count_DGEmatrix.txt.gz"
    ),
    "reference": (
        "https://datasets.cellxgene.cziscience.com/"
        "a420c2bf-feeb-48db-a6c7-71f492f23131.h5ad"
    ),
}

raw_dir = Path("data/raw")
raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

source_paths = {}
for source_name, source_url in source_urls.items():
    source_path = raw_dir / Path(source_url).name
    if not source_path.exists():
        urlretrieve(source_url, source_path)
    source_paths[source_name] = source_path
    print(f"{source_name}: {source_path.name}  ({source_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.0f} MB)")

dge_path = source_paths["dge"]
reference_path = source_paths["reference"]
```

## Build the AnnData

```{python}
#| label: create-anndata
adata_path = Path("data/processed/GSE150703_adata.h5ad")
adata_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

if adata_path.exists():
    adata = sc.read_h5ad(adata_path)
else:
    counts = pd.read_csv(dge_path, sep="\t", index_col=0).T

    adata = ad.AnnData(X=csr_matrix(counts.values))
    adata.obs_names = counts.index.astype(str)
    adata.var_names = counts.columns.astype(str)

    fields = pd.Series(adata.obs_names).str.split("_", expand=True)
    adata.obs["condition"] = pd.Categorical(fields[0].values)
    adata.obs["timepoint"] = pd.Categorical(fields[1].values)
    adata.obs["sort"] = pd.Categorical(fields[2].values)
    adata.obs["lab"] = pd.Categorical(fields[3].values)
    adata.obs["replicate"] = pd.Categorical(fields[4].values)
    adata.obs["batch"] = pd.Categorical(fields[2].str.cat(fields[3], sep="_").values)

    adata.write_h5ad(adata_path)

adata
```

## Reference centroids

```{python}
#| label: reference-centroids
# MRCA, the mouse retina cell atlas (330,930 cells, all of it disease-free):
# https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2024.109916. Its majorclass column is the level the calls
# come from — twelve classes, about what twenty clusters can resolve.
#
# Aggregated over the whole atlas rather than its P14/P17 cells alone. That subset looks
# like the right match for this design, but it holds no astrocytes at all, 50 RGCs, and
# bipolar cells almost only at P17, so it cannot call several of the clusters here.
centroid_path = Path("data/processed/MRCA_majorclass_centroids.h5ad")

if centroid_path.exists():
    reference_centroids = sc.read_h5ad(centroid_path)
else:
    # read_h5ad would also pull in .raw, which is a second copy of an already 9.8 GB matrix
    # and takes the load past this machine's memory. Only the three elements the aggregation
    # needs are read, and the indices are narrowed to int32 — they index 31,671 columns.
    with h5py.File(reference_path) as handle:
        reference_counts = read_elem(handle["X"])
        reference_obs = read_elem(handle["obs"])
        reference_var = read_elem(handle["var"])

    reference_counts.indices = reference_counts.indices.astype(np.int32)
    reference_counts.indptr = reference_counts.indptr.astype(np.int32)

    reference = ad.AnnData(
        X=reference_counts,
        obs=reference_obs[["majorclass"]],
        var=reference_var[["feature_name"]],
    )
    del reference_counts, reference_obs, reference_var

    reference_centroids = sc.get.aggregate(reference, by="majorclass", func="mean")
    reference_centroids.X = reference_centroids.layers.pop("mean")
    del reference

    # the atlas is keyed on Ensembl ids and the query on upper-cased symbols. Nine symbols
    # answer to more than one id; those are dropped rather than merged, since there is no
    # honest way to pick which id the query's column meant.
    symbols = reference_centroids.var["feature_name"].astype(str).str.upper()
    reference_centroids = reference_centroids[:, ~symbols.duplicated(keep=False).to_numpy()].copy()
    reference_centroids.var_names = symbols[~symbols.duplicated(keep=False)].to_numpy()

    reference_centroids.write_h5ad(centroid_path)

# keyed on every class in the reference rather than only the ones called, so a cell type
# keeps its colour across both batches whatever each one happens to find
cell_type_palette = dict(zip(sorted(reference_centroids.obs_names), sc.pl.palettes.default_20))

reference_centroids
```

:::

```{python}
#| label: analyse-batches
# ── everything that happens to the data, in order, for each batch ──
for batch, settings in BATCHES.items():
    display(Markdown(f"# {batch}"))

    batch_adata = cluster_batch(adata, batch)
    for obs_key, palette in obs_palettes.items():
        batch_adata.uns[f"{obs_key}_colors"] = [
            palette[category] for category in batch_adata.obs[obs_key].cat.categories
        ]

    resolution_keys = [column for column in batch_adata.obs.columns if column.endswith("_v0")]
    for leiden_key_v0 in resolution_keys:
        batch_adata.uns[f"{leiden_key_v0}_colors"] = [
            mcolors.to_hex(plt.cm.tab20.colors[int(category) % 20])
            for category in batch_adata.obs[leiden_key_v0].cat.categories
        ]

    umap_sweep_slide(batch_adata, resolution_keys)

    ranked_key = rank_clusters(batch_adata, settings["resolution"])
    html_section(
        "Chosen resolution",
        f"`{ranked_key}`: {batch_adata.obs[ranked_key].nunique()} clusters",
        as_table(batch_adata.obs[ranked_key].value_counts()),
    )

    umap_clusters_slide(batch_adata, ranked_key)

    qc_df = sc.get.obs_df(batch_adata, keys=[ranked_key] + list(qc_metrics))
    qc_violin_slide(batch_adata, qc_df)
    qc_violin_by_cluster_slide(batch_adata, qc_df, ranked_key)

    reference_correlation, n_feature_genes = correlate_with_reference(
        batch_adata, ranked_key, reference_centroids
    )
    html_section(
        "Correlation with the reference",
        f"{n_feature_genes} of {int(batch_adata.var['highly_variable'].sum())} "
        f"variable genes found in the reference",
        as_table(reference_correlation.round(3)),
    )
    heatmap_reference_slide(reference_correlation)

    markers_present, marker_report = score_markers(batch_adata)
    html_section("Marker scores", as_text(marker_report))

    score_df = sc.get.obs_df(batch_adata, keys=[ranked_key] + score_keys)
    score_violin_by_cluster_slide(batch_adata, score_df, ranked_key)
    umap_scores_slide(batch_adata)
    dotplot_markers_slide(batch_adata, markers_present, ranked_key)

    mean_scores = score_df.groupby(ranked_key, observed=True)[score_keys].mean()
    mean_scores.columns = [cell_type.replace("_", " ") for cell_type in retina_markers]
    heatmap_scores_slide(mean_scores)

    # the call is the best-correlating reference class, overridden by the sheet at the top.
    # The marker scores stay in the document as an independent read on the same question.
    cluster_calls = reference_correlation.idxmax(axis=1)
    marker_calls = mean_scores.idxmax(axis=1)
    cluster_calls.update(pd.Series(settings["overrides"]))

    batch_adata.obs["cell_type"] = batch_adata.obs[ranked_key].map(cluster_calls).astype("category")
    batch_adata.uns["cell_type_colors"] = [
        cell_type_palette[cell_type] for cell_type in batch_adata.obs["cell_type"].cat.categories
    ]

    # margin is the gap to the runner-up class: a cluster called on a hair's difference is
    # one to read the heatmap for, however high its correlation
    sorted_correlation = np.sort(reference_correlation.to_numpy(), axis=1)
    call_table = pd.DataFrame({
        "cell_type": cluster_calls,
        "cells": batch_adata.obs[ranked_key].value_counts(),
        "correlation": reference_correlation.max(axis=1).round(3),
        "margin": (sorted_correlation[:, -1] - sorted_correlation[:, -2]).round(3),
        "marker call": marker_calls,
    })
    html_section("Cell types called", as_table(call_table))

    refinements, diagnostics = refine_cell_types(
        batch_adata, ranked_key, cluster_calls, marker_calls, cell_type_palette
    )
    # a rejected row is not a failure: the cluster keeps its whole-cluster call, and the
    # row is the record of the panel having been overruled
    html_section(
        "Refining a call with the marker scores",
        as_table(diagnostics.set_index("cluster")) if len(diagnostics)
        else "No cluster was called differently by the reference and the panel.",
        as_table(batch_adata.obs["cell_type"].value_counts()),
    )
    refine_scatter_slide(batch_adata, refinements, diagnostics, ranked_key, cell_type_palette)

    umap_cell_types_slide(batch_adata)

    txn1_df = sc.get.obs_df(batch_adata, keys=["TXN1", "cell_type", "condition", "timepoint"])
    umap_txn1_slide(batch_adata)
    txn1_violin_celltype_slide(batch_adata, txn1_df, cell_type_palette)
    txn1_violin_condition_slide(batch_adata, txn1_df)
    txn1_violin_timepoint_slide(batch_adata, txn1_df)
    umap_txn1_stratified_slide(batch_adata)
    txn1_violin_stratified_slide(batch_adata, txn1_df)
    txn1_violin_stratified_by_condition_slide(batch_adata, txn1_df)

    del batch_adata
```
